title: Exact $k$-Center Clustering on Graphs for Small $k$

problem.claim: The work addresses k-center clustering on graphs used in data mining tasks including prototype selection, facility placement, and dataset summarization.

gap.claim: Practitioners largely rely on approximation algorithms or heuristics because exact computation is perceived as impractical.

contributions.claim: Introduces an exact algorithm for k-center clustering in the small-k regime, borrowing concepts from LP-type optimization.
Provides theoretical justification for the proposed approach.
Reports that exact k-center can be practical for interesting classes of real-world datasets in the small-k regime.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the practicability of their approach.
The authors report findings that challenge the assumption that exact k-center is impractical and establish a practical regime for optimal clustering.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based k-center clustering supports several data mining tasks.
Exact computation is generally avoided in favor of approximations or heuristics because it is considered impractical.
The paper introduces a new LP-type-inspired exact algorithm targeting the small-k regime.
The authors provide theoretical justification and extensive experiments.
The reported findings challenge the conventional impracticality assumption and identify a practical regime for optimal clustering.

source_observation.claim: Exact optimization may become practical when the problem is restricted to a small-k regime.

interpretation.claim: Problem-parameter restrictions can create a practically useful regime for exact methods.

application.claim: Consider exact clustering for applications whose number of centers is small before defaulting to approximation or heuristics.

exception.claim: The abstract limits the claim to the small-k regime and interesting classes of real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact algorithmic formulation or complexity guarantees.
The abstract does not identify the dataset classes, baselines, experimental metrics, or quantitative results.
